Quick decisions we recommend today:
- Preferred connector: PrivateLink if you want managed endpoints and explicit per-service authorization. VPC Peering can be faster for heavy egress/throughput but requires route management on both sides. (Aditya will outline tradeoffs below).
- Egress IPs: Redwood can provide a small pool of static egress IPs for outbound traffic; if you need vendor-level allowlists we’ll reserve them during provisioning.

4) Redwood NetOps: Validate MTU and recommended subnet sizing for peering if you choose that path — Karthik (3 business days).
5) Procurement intro & SOW draft — Redwood Sales Ops & Finly Procurement (linked).

Staging timeline if we get the CIDR by 11/04 and procurement is not blocked:
- Week 1: Exchange config + Redwood config ready (PrivateLink service registered)
- Week 2: Customer endpoint creation and connectivity test with synthetic traffic
- Week 3: Full test with sample traffic, allowlist verification, and handoff to Finly devs

I'll follow up with the PrivateLink vs Peering one-pager and a short checklist for our infra team. For now, please confirm the CIDR and whether your security team prefers PrivateLink or wants us to scope peering.

Subject: Re: Finly POC — technical note on PrivateLink vs Peering

Paul — quick technical note to help decide: we usually recommend PrivateLink when customers need
- strong per-service access controls (IAM + endpoint policies),
- minimal route table changes on their VPC,
- simplified audit trails (connections appear as endpoint service events).

Peering is attractive if you expect sustained multi-GPU traffic (high throughput) and prefer native VPC routing without the proxy layer. Caveats: no transitive routing, and you have to manage route propagation and security groups carefully.

On egress: our managed Private VPC offering can allocate a small, static set of outbound IPs (NATs in our account or yours depending on model). If you need guaranteed dedicated IPs for vendor allowlisting, we can reserve them during provisioning but that adds a small allocation step in week 1.

I've attached a short brief with diagrams (redwood-private-vpc-brief.pdf). If you confirm PrivateLink, Karthik will send the endpoint-service name and ARN so your infra can create the endpoint.

Regards,
Aditya Rao
Solution Architect — Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-private-vpc-brief.pdf
